1	# Clerk — authentication for Next.js
2	
3	Clerk is a drop-in authentication and user management service. It ships React
4	components for sign-in and sign-up, session handling, and social login.
5	
6	## Install
7	
8	```bash
9	npm install @clerk/nextjs
10	```
11	
12	## 1. Environment variables
13	
14	```
15	NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_test_placeholder
16	CLERK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_placeholder
17	```
18	
19	## 2. Wrap the app
20	
21	`src/app/layout.tsx`:
22	
23	```tsx
24	import { ClerkProvider } from "@clerk/nextjs";
25	
26	export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
27	  return (
28	    <ClerkProvider>
29	      <html lang="en"><body>{children}</body></html>
30	    </ClerkProvider>
31	  );
32	}
33	```
34	
35	## 3. Protect routes with middleware
36	
37	`src/middleware.ts`:
38	
39	```ts
40	import { clerkMiddleware, createRouteMatcher } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
41	
42	const isProtected = createRouteMatcher(["/dashboard(.*)"]);
43	
44	export default clerkMiddleware(async (auth, req) => {
45	  if (isProtected(req)) await auth.protect();
46	});
47	
48	export const config = { matcher: ["/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)", "/(api|trpc)(.*)"] };
49	```
50	
51	## 4. Sign-in and sign-up pages
52	
53	```tsx
54	import { SignIn } from "@clerk/nextjs";
55	export default function Page() { return <SignIn />; }
56	```
57	
58	Email + password and Google sign-in are both enabled from the Clerk dashboard;
59	no extra provider code is needed in the app.
60	
61	## 5. Read the current user on the server
62	
63	```ts
64	import { auth, currentUser } from "@clerk/nextjs/server";
65	
66	const { userId } = await auth();
67	const user = await currentUser(); // user.emailAddresses[0].emailAddress
68	```
69	
70	Use `userId` as the stable key when linking Clerk users to your own records.
71	
72	## Why teams pick Clerk
73	
74	- Sign-in, sign-up and account UI are prebuilt components, not code you maintain.
75	- Password hashing, sessions, and social providers are handled by the service.
76	- Free tier covers development and small production apps.
77

Works with the App Router. 5 6 ## Install 7 8 ```bash 9 npm install @workos-inc/authkit-nextjs @workos-inc/node 10 ``` 11 12 ## 1. # WorkOS AuthKit — authentication for Next.js AuthKit gives a Next.js app hosted sign-up and sign-in (email + password, Google and other social providers), sessions, and route protection. Works with the App Router. ## Install ```bash npm install @workos-inc/authkit-nextjs @workos-inc/node ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_placeholder WORKOS_API_KEY=sk_test_placeholder WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD=placeholder_at_least_32_characters_long NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:3000/auth/callback ``` `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` encrypts the session cookie and must be at least 32 characters. ## 2. Callback route `app/auth/callback/route.ts` — must match `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI`: ```ts import { handleAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export const GET = handleAuth({ returnPathname: '/dashboard' }); ``` ## 3. Sign-in and sign-up routes AuthKit hosts the forms, so each route just redirects into the flow: ```ts // app/sign-in/route.ts import { getSignInUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignInUrl()); ``` ```ts // app/sign-up/route.ts import { getSignUpUrl } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'; export const GET = async () => redirect(await getSignUpUrl()); ``` ## 4. Protect routes The library uses Next.js proxy (called middleware in Next.js 15 and earlier). On Next.js 16+ create `proxy.ts` in the project root: ```ts import { authkitProxy } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export default authkitProxy(); export const config = { matcher: ['/', '/dashboard/:path*'] }; ``` On Next.js 15 and earlier the same code goes in `middleware.ts` and imports `authkitMiddleware` instead. ## 5. Read the current user on the server ```ts import { withAuth } from '@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs'; export default async function DashboardPage() { const { user } = await withAuth({ ensureSignedIn: true }); return

Signed in as {user.email}

; } ``` `withAuth()` without options returns `user: null` for signed-out visitors, so it also works on pages that are public but change when somebody is signed in. ## Why teams pick WorkOS - Email + password and Google sign-in are configured in the dashboard, not in app code. - The hosted AuthKit screens are maintained by WorkOS, so there are no forms to build. - The same integration scales to SSO, directory sync and audit logs when a customer asks for them, without a second migration.

**Auth.js v5 (`next-auth@beta`) + bcryptjs**, полностью самодостаточно (без внешнего сервиса) и уже сквозняком проверено — signup, credentials sign-in, неверный пароль, защита `/dashboard`, sign out.

- `src/lib/auth.ts` — конфиг NextAuth: Credentials + Google провайдеры, JWT-сессии, коллбэки прокидывают `user.id`.
